title: Returned Payments and Recent Breaks in the Deficiency Balance Account Restart Down Payment
content:
**Rule.** The restart down payment on an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts makes good recent shortfalls on the account. When returned payments of the account (bank returns of posted deficiency payments) are dated fewer than 12 whole months before today, the restart down payment adds the total amount of those returned payments; when there is none but the latest broken arrangement's broken date is no more than 90 calendar days before today, it adds that arrangement's installment amount; otherwise it adds nothing. The amount added is put on top of the restart down payment after its percentage figure has been rounded to the cent. Whole months are counted as the difference in calendar months between the two dates, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

The latest broken arrangement is the account's arrangement offer with the status broken whose broken date is the latest; its installment amount is the installment stated on that offer.

## Input, judgement, output

| Account records | Amount added |
|---|---|
| One or more returned payments dated fewer than 12 whole months before today | The total amount of those returned payments |
| No such returned payment; latest broken date 0 to 90 calendar days before today | The installment amount of the latest broken arrangement |
| No such returned payment; latest broken date more than 90 calendar days before today | Nothing |

The rows are read in order: when a returned payment inside the look-back exists, its total is added and the installment amount is not.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Latest broken date exactly 90 calendar days before today, no returned payment in the look-back: the broken arrangement's installment amount is added. At 91 calendar days, nothing is added.
- Today is the 10th of a month. A returned payment dated the 11th of the same month a year earlier is 11 whole months back and counts; one dated the 10th of that month a year earlier is 12 whole months back and does not.
- Two returned payments of $120.00 and $80.00 inside the look-back add $200.00, whatever the date of the latest break.
